_source: registry.d/apt-retired.json — the eight still-enabled apt entries that CANNOT be expressed in the one install format, disabled with a per-app reason. Staged for the single writer of registry.json. See roadmap/INSTALL-METHODOLOGY.md §7.
_why_disabled_not_deleted: An entry that is refused at install time but still LISTED is the worse of the two failures: the App Hub offers a button that always errors. `_disabled` makes InstallFromRegistry refuse by name before anything else runs, and keeps the curated metadata (arch, keywords, icon, the reason) on disk so re-enabling any of these is one field, not a fresh investigation. Deleting them would throw away the only record of why they are gone.
_honest_cost: This is a REAL product loss: eight apps leave the catalogue, and jupyter and jellyfin are the two most likely to be missed. Nothing here claims they were replaced.
_signing: UNSIGNED BY CONSTRUCTION. Every entry carries "signature": "" and is inert until `make sign-registry` is run by the founder.

cockpit.name: Cockpit
cockpit.description: Web-based server management — terminal, logs, processes, networking, storage, and system monitoring in one dashboard
cockpit.author: Red Hat / Cockpit Project
cockpit._note: PARKED BY THE INSTALL-METHODOLOGY MIGRATION, 2026-08-17. cockpit is a Debian-integrated system component (cockpit-ws, -bridge, -system, -networkmanager, -storaged, -packagekit) that installs into /usr/lib and talks to systemd and PackageKit on the host. Upstream publishes no self-contained per-architecture artefact, so there is nothing to pin. If Vulos wants a Cockpit-like panel it belongs in the base image, not in a per-app catalogue that installs into $HOME/.vulos/apps. Its `install` shell string is left in place verbatim rather than blanked: the installer refuses it loudly (INSTALL-01) and the string is the record of what the app used to need. `_disabled` is what actually stops it, and it is reversible in one edit.

latest.install: apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends cockpit cockpit-ws cockpit-bridge cockpit-system cockpit-networkmanager cockpit-storaged cockpit-packagekit

httpbin.name: httpbin
httpbin.description: HTTP request and response testing — inspect headers, methods, status codes
httpbin.author: Kenneth Reitz
httpbin._note: PARKED BY THE INSTALL-METHODOLOGY MIGRATION, 2026-08-17. httpbin was `pip3 install --break-system-packages httpbin gunicorn`. pip is a package manager with the SAME unpinned-resolution problem as apt — `pip install httpbin` on two days gives two httpbins — so swapping one for the other would trade nothing. There is no single pinned artefact for a Python app plus its dependency tree, and building one is a wheel-bundling project, not a recipe edit. Its `install` shell string is left in place verbatim rather than blanked: the installer refuses it loudly (INSTALL-01) and the string is the record of what the app used to need. `_disabled` is what actually stops it, and it is reversible in one edit.

0.9.install: apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends python3-pip python3 && pip3 install --break-system-packages httpbin gunicorn

jellyfin.name: Jellyfin
jellyfin.description: Free self-hosted media server — stream movies, TV shows, music, and photos to any device via a web UI; replaces VLC for media playback
jellyfin.author: Jellyfin Contributors
jellyfin._note: PARKED BY THE INSTALL-METHODOLOGY MIGRATION, 2026-08-17. NOT migrated, and the reason is honest ignorance rather than absence. jellyfin DOES publish pinnable per-architecture portable tarballs and their URLs were confirmed to exist by HTTP HEAD on 2026-08-17 — repo.jellyfin.org/files/server/linux/stable/v10.11.11/{amd64,arm64}/jellyfin_10.11.11-{amd64,arm64}.tar.gz, 110228765 and 107416274 bytes. They were NOT downloaded and NOT hashed, and two things were not measured: whether the portable build is self-contained or needs a .NET runtime the image does not carry, and whether ffmpeg is present. An entry pinned on an unhashed URL is a fabricated checksum waiting to happen, so it is parked with the URLs recorded. This is the cheapest of the eight to finish. Its `install` shell string is left in place verbatim rather than blanked: the installer refuses it loudly (INSTALL-01) and the string is the record of what the app used to need. `_disabled` is what actually stops it, and it is reversible in one edit.

10.install: apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends apt-transport-https curl gnupg && curl -fsSL https://repo.jellyfin.org/debian/jellyfin_team.gpg.key | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/jellyfin.gpg && echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/jellyfin.gpg] https://repo.jellyfin.org/debian bookworm main' > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/jellyfin.list && apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends jellyfin-server jellyfin-web
